title: Core: Use canonical links in sidebar and menu
body:
## What I did

* Transforms buttons in menu and sidebar into `a` when relevant 
* Adds `rel="canonical"` attr to help crawlers index our content

comments.body:
_⚠️ Potential issue_ | _🟡 Minor_

**Remove `rel="canonical"` from sidebar navigation links.**

The `rel="canonical"` attribute is designed for SEO canonicalization—specifying the preferred URL when duplicate content exists across multiple URLs. Sidebar navigation links (DocumentNode, StoryLeafNode, TestNode) point to distinct stories with unique content, not duplicates. Using canonical tags on these navigation elements provides no SEO benefit and is semantically incorrect.

Also applies to: 183-183, 200-200

<details>
<summary>🤖 Prompt for AI Agents</summary>

```
In code/core/src/manager/components/sidebar/TreeNode.tsx around lines 143, 183,
and 200, the sidebar navigation links incorrectly include rel="canonical";
remove the rel="canonical" attribute from those
LeafNode/DocumentNode/StoryLeafNode/TestNode JSX elements so the navigation
links no longer emit canonical link hints. Search the file for any other
instances of rel="canonical" on sidebar link components and delete those
attributes (or stop passing them via props) to ensure semantic correctness and
no unintended SEO effects.
```

</details>

comments.author: Sidnioulz
comments.body: Our URLs use query params and are therefore not treated as canonical by default. Adding canonical is the whole point of the PR.

comments.author: Sidnioulz
comments.body: - [ ] Mobile navigation buttons need to be ported too

comments.author: ndelangen
comments.body:
Does this code get re-evaluated upon every story navigation?
I suspect it doesn't.

So this `href` would upon load be correct, but afterwards as the user navigates become outdated.

Though I suspect it isn't breaking, it's very unexpected, and likely would lead to bugs in the future.

I'm wondering if it's worth introducing, or or not.

comments.author: Sidnioulz
comments.body:
Good catch :fishing_pole_and_fish:

I'd prefer to have these be proper links (which requires a `href`). Should I read the current story in this menu to force it to recompute hrefs?

If we do want to drop this though, it's not _strictly necessary_ for SEO (just good for UX and accessibility), so that can help limit the amount of changes in the module.

comments.author: ndelangen
comments.body:
I've seen designs from @MichaelArestad where these items no longer existed in the menu.
It's likely not really worth investing too much time in getting the URL right then.

I propose keeping the `href` something like `#next-story` and `#previous-component` and the onClick will actually navigate.

Then if it becomes clear the option will not be removed, we could invest time in handling those hash-navigation events globally?
Or find a way to keep re-rendering the menu (make it subscribe to state).

What do you think?

comments.author: Sidnioulz
comments.body:
I think having fake URLs would be more damaging (also to our SEO as we'd be advertising false URLs to crawlers).

I'll disable the `href`s for now and we'll see if this survives the next menu iteration and take it from there.

comments.author: ghengeveld
comments.body: Looks like you're redefining an already existing variable `refId`. Looks like you don't need this actually.

comments.author: ghengeveld
comments.body: It would be better to use `asChild` (with an `a` child element) rather than `as='a'`.

comments.author: Sidnioulz
comments.body: Try and use Link, and make link show href but call nav when `internal`. Also add `canonical` boolean prop

comments.author: Sidnioulz
comments.body: This could have side effects on existing Links in users' MDX so I'll abstain.
